The pipeline is now LIVE AND VERIFIED — this round reviews shipped state, per the after-the-fact-by-design ruling. ROUND-2 DISPOSITIONS, each with what changed: (1) PRIOR_ART (high, gating) + DEBUG_HISTORIAN (medium): the seat was RIGHT and my claim was a false asserted-absence — run-migrations.sh's own header names docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/ as its migrations home, schema_migrations IS the ledger, and my raw-psql apply had left 342 pending-forever (bugs_open/007's replay trap). 342 is now recorded via --record-only with an honest note; the checksum was re-synced after this round's hardening edits; the false claim is logged in WRONG_CALLS with the five-line check that would have avoided it. (2) EDITQUALITY (medium): the system.internal dependency is no longer an unverified assumption — the seed's in-transaction DO/RAISE now refuses to apply into a database with no sites row for domain=system.internal (a missing row previously degraded every filing to log-only, silently). Re-applied; assert passes. (3) EDITQUALITY (low, doc_notes): confirmed explicitly — the doc_notes write is raw SQL inside the seed, routed through no Go writer, so only the DB CHECK constraint applies, and subject_type='pipeline' is in its allowed set (schema read live). (4) EDITQUALITY (low, category): both registry entries recategorised training→maintenance, matching the work items' pipeline value. (5) GUARDIAN (medium): the generic-topic workflow-selection question now has a DEFINITIVE answer, not an analogy — the thunder-orphan-scan itself ran on exactly that path today: scheduler fired config.agent_type=thunder-orphan-scan onto system.agent.generic.requests, extractGroupInfo (processor.go:1074) selected the right workflow, and the run COMPLETED at 11:42:06Z with its own two steps executed. (6) GUARDIAN (low, registry collision): additive string keys in a Go map literal — a collision is a compile error; HEAD builds green with both entries. (7) DEBUG_HISTORIAN (low): defensive ROLLBACK now heads the seed, and 342_thunder_orphan_scan_ROLLBACK.sql ships as the sidecar (runner's SIDECAR_RE excludes it from apply; it reverts the three seeded rows and deliberately leaves any thunder_orphan work items for a human to read first). NEW SINCE ROUND 2, FOUND BY THE FIRST LIVE RUN AND FIXED: my round-2 sketch asserted the awaited response lands at collected_data.<output_field>.response, 'verified against the live reaper run'. That was WRONG, and the guardian's round-1 low-severity wiring objection had pointed at exactly it: the coordinator stores an awaited response under the STEP NAME, plus the STEP-LEVEL output_field only (models.Step parses stepMap[output_field], processor.go:434) — and a config-nested output_field, which my seed carried by copying the reaper's shape, is parsed by NOTHING (the reaper's own nested copy has been silently inert since it shipped; its step name and output_field are word-reversals, so the specimen I 'verified' against could never have discriminated). The first live run failed at reconcile on this; the seed now declares output_field at step level (with a DO/RAISE assert so the inert form cannot silently return), the run was repeated and COMPLETED, a LANDMINES entry was filed (verifier dispatched) and a WRONG_CALLS entry records the non-discriminating verification. LIVE-VERIFIED STATE: fleet v1.0.1273 carries all code (pod-grepped, both chassis replicas + adapter, positive and spelling-negative controls); seed applied AND ledger-recorded; first successful scan COMPLETED 11:42:06Z with counts truthful against the same-session independent checks (vendor_billing 0 = manual instances/list {}; db_rows 23 / db_live 0 = direct table read; clean=true — a 0-findings run that PROVED it looked). The filing path remains exercised only to the classification boundary (no real orphan has existed to file); this is disclosed in the register entry and the seed's first-run notes. ORIGINAL CASE unchanged: provision writes thunder_instances only after the vendor box is up, so a crash in that window or a hand-created instance bills invisibly; the sweep reconciles against vendor truth every 6h, read-and-report, no remediation authority.

The one-off double-fire at a hand-kicked first tick (last_triggered_at=NULL) is absorbed by dedup but unexplained at the scheduler-stamp level; it did not recur across subsequent ticks and a 6h interval makes it negligible — noted, not chased.
